note: Contrarian Shark, skeptical-researcher angle. The draft restates five locked surfaces, remaps them to four, then treats stub-green, best-effort writes, and skippable Playwright as if they identified the claim. Fresh-context only — judged against the locked criteria, not the codebase.

findings.criterion: 1 — When a Gandalf run finalizes, a researchPrime / lane job finishes, or a Foreman wave GOes, one row is appended
findings.message: Criterion 1 names three finish events as the surface, and the third is not “Foreman finishes.” It is “a Foreman wave GOes.” The plan HOLDs Hook C′ and the elegance pass argues CUT because Hook C will register the execution log once at RUN_DONE. That substitutes the statement’s example artifact for the criterion’s trigger. A five-wave build that GOes four times and then dies never fires finish_run, so under CUT/HOLD the register is empty for the whole life of the run — the opposite of “wave GOes → one row.” Calling the locked criterion “proposer-written” so it can be dropped is a North Star rewrite, not a cut. Re-asking John “live per-wave or once at finish?” re-opens a lock. Wire the wave-GO row, or amend criterion 1. As written, the third trigger is not implementable and not measured.

findings.criterion: 3 — Both places, one source; a report registered with a step shows under that step in the plan outline, and the tile always shows it
findings.message: Criterion 3 is a join: the outline lists “the step’s register rows (already keyed by the register’s step column).” Criterion 1 also requires “the roadmap step it belongs to (the active step at the time).” Hook A (Gandalf, the named example) and Hook B (lane jobs) call register() with what/where/date and do not pass step. register()’s signature defaults step=None; the draft never says the function fills a missing step from active_step(). The helper itself is two key spaces: “hint (step id/name) wins” else “1-based index (what stepDeliverables matches by number).” A name that wins cannot join a numeric outline. There is no test that a Gandalf row’s step cell equals the outline’s join key. Phase 4 then asserts the row appears under the active step — that is the hypothesis, not a write-side contract. If Foreman copies Hook A as written, the named report lands on the tile and is invisible in the outline, which is exactly half of “two places at once.”

findings.criterion: 1 — one row is appended when a run finishes
findings.message: Criterion 1 is a count: one row per finish. Hook B obeys it (one `/report/` per job). Hook C does not: “for each doc the session persisted (effort_history.efforts_for_session_id + summarizer.session_doc_roles) register one row.” session_doc_roles is a role map (exec/report/agent/provenance/master/impl/execlog). That is N rows, including computer-facing files the 2026-09-05 quote never named. The elegance HOLD (“human-facing report/plan/execlog only”) is a parenthetical the near-term specifics do not implement; a builder following the body still blasts. Idempotency on (what, where) does not collapse a run to one row when where is a different file each time. The plan therefore cannot say what “one row” means on the steward path John actually uses. Pick a grain — one row per finished run, pointing at the human artifact — and gate it; the blast is not that grain.

findings.criterion: 5 — a Gandalf run on a real project is opened from the plan outline AND the deliverables tile on the page; a run: row opens a terminal with the command staged (Playwright screenshots), before v1.2.13
findings.message: Criterion 5 is a claim about John’s page, not about pytest staying green. The only surface proof is `tests/test_register_links_playwright_2026_09_05.py` with `importorskip`, plus a release checklist that “live-verifies.” importorskip means the steward/cockpit nets named in the same criterion can pass while Playwright never ran. The Gandalf half waits on a live model finalize with no named timeout, no named “Bottom line” budget, and no rule that a skip or a degraded Gandalf blocks v1.2.13. The run: half plants a hand-written smoke row — it does not observe a finish hook writing `run:` — so a screenshot of a staged command does not identify “a finished run registers itself” and “opens from both places” together. File-presence of a PNG is the v4 failure class this phase cites and then reimplements. Name a non-skippable ship rule that the two clicks and the unsent command are on the page, or criterion 5 remains a procedure.

findings.criterion: 2 — a Where cell that is /report/… or /artifact/… is openable; rows pointing outside the effort AND outside Anchor’s routes still render as text (containment stands)
findings.message: The classifier returns a route when every `/report/` segment matches `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+`. The character class includes `.`, so `..` is a legal segment. The STUB GATE simultaneously asserts `/report/<pid>/../x` → `openable=False` / `route=None`. Those two sentences cannot both be the spec. Containment is the locked risk row (“only Anchor’s own contained routes qualify; anything else stays text”), and the test is the only mechanical gate. A builder who implements the regex ships a route the test claims is text; a builder who implements the test writes a reject the regex does not mention. Until `..` and `.` are named exclusions in the grammar the test compiles against, criterion 2 is not identified — the gate and the rule measure different strings.

findings.criterion: 4 — Run link opens a cockpit terminal in the project’s tree with the command staged as a pending paste (Enter runs it); 5 — a run: row opens a terminal with the command staged
findings.message: The North Star’s dependent variable is the command sitting unsent on the shell prompt so Enter runs it. The plan operationalizes “prompt” as “the PTY has produced its first prompt bytes (any output).” First bytes from `%COMSPEC%`/PowerShell are banner, profile, or a working-directory warning — not `PS …>`. Flushing raw bytes into that stream (no bracketed paste, no trailing newline) can land the command in the middle of startup text. Enter then does not run the staged command as a unit, which is the failure mode the risk table (“never submits”) does not even name. The stub PTY “emits immediately,” so the once-only / no-`\

findings.criterion: 1 — when a run finalizes, one row is appended to the effort’s DELIVERABLES.md
findings.message: The Why Now of this North Star is that listing a human artifact is currently a hope because nothing writes the row. The proposed fix is a function that “Never raises (best-effort, returns the reason)” plus a journal field `{register: written|dup|reason}`. A successful Gandalf/lane/commission finish can therefore still leave DELIVERABLES.md unchanged, and the surface John reads (outline + tile) has no failure state — only a log line. Tests pin cancelled/failed → no row and duplicate → one row; they do not pin “STATUS_DONE + register() returns written:false” as a visible miss. Journaling a silent no-op makes the miss auditable, not true. Criterion 1 is not “we tried.” Until a successful run with a failed write is a failed surface (or a hard, retried write), the convention remains a hope with better logs.

findings.criterion: 1 — one row appended when a Foreman wave GOes; risk row — a run with no effort context still lands a row at the project root
findings.message: The locked risk table already decided the no-effort case: “the project root is the effort of record; the row lands there.” Phase 2 then defers the entire uncommissioned-terminal Foreman path (“registers only at close/kill… wiring into close_session/kill is deferred… keep the W6 close path untouched”). Those two sentences cannot be true together. Classic window jobs are the risk row’s example, not an exotic follow-on. Hook B also refuses `lane not in ('research','plan')`, so a launch_lane build never registers either. After CUT/HOLD of C′ and this deferral, the only Foreman row in the plan is steward-commissioned finish_run. That is not the criterion, and it is not the mitigation the lock already chose.

findings.criterion: 4 — Documents keep their open link; nothing else changes
findings.message: The parser asserts “a row may have BOTH an open target and a run command.” Criterion 4 requires the document Open link to survive when `run:` is present. The only round-trip on run: is a planted `| smoke: prints hi | run: python -c "print('hi')" |` row with no route/path in Where. Documents-without-run: are byte-identical regression tests; BOTH is untested on parse, on delivRow (Open ↗ and Run ▶ together), and on the page. The 5th-column scan is also a schema change the non-goal parked. If Where is a route plus a `run:` suffix, Phase 4 never clicks that Open link. The property is stated; no gate can see it fail.

findings.criterion: 2 — the pane and the plan outline render the route as a link that opens in a new window
findings.message: Openable `/artifact/<pid>?path=<rel>` already carries a query string. The renderer is specified as “token appended exactly as the deliverable-file link does at :458–462.” That existing append is unidentified for a URL that already has `?`. A naive `?token=` produces a second `?` (token dropped or path broken); a missing `&token=` opens a new window that 401s. Criterion 2’s “opens” is then a 401 tab, which the STUB GATE never hits — it only classifies the Where cell, it does not GET the href. Name the join (`&token=` on query-bearing routes, `?token=` otherwise) and assert the clicked URL is authed, or “openable” is a CSS link to an unusable window.
